newsitem.title: LATVIA: STOCKS CLOSE TO FEB LOWS, UNIBANKA DOWN.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS CLOSE TO FEB LOWS, UNIBANKA DOWN.

text.p: * Most shares were weaker today and total turnover came to 57,700 lats compared with 92,000 lats, close to early February lows of 52,000 lats.
* Saule10 index was down 0.7 pct to 150.01.
* Daugavpils Chain of the secondary list was the most traded stock as it slipped five santimes to 2.40 lats on volume of 17,300 lats.
* Unibanka slipped again to 3.47 lats from 3.50 lats on trade of 6,500 lats after regaining some ground last session.
* Valmiera Glassfibre was among the few gainers. It rose to 1.54 lats from 1.47 lats on 3,800 lats.
Latvian stocks were mostly weaker on Thursday, close to early February lows, and more funds were seen trickling out of the bourse, dealers said.
However, some revival was expected as companies reveal their first quarter results, dealers said.
Turnover came to 57,700 lats compared with 92,000 lats. Early February lowest levels came to some 52,000 lats of volume.
Saules Bank's index Saule10 was down 0.7 percent to 150.01.
"The fall is not so sharp any more although funds are still trickling out of the bourse," Uldis Bulavs, a dealer with Trasta Bank, told Reuters.
"In May I would expect more life or at least stabilisation of prices as more first quarter results come in," he added.
Leading share Unibanka slipped again to 3.47 lats from 3.50 lats on 6,500 lats after regaining ground in the last session.
Daugavpils Chain on the secondary list was the most traded stock as it slipped five santimes to 2.40 lats on volume of 17,300 lats.
Valmiera Glassfibre was among the few gainers today as it advanced to 1.54 lats from 1.47 lats on 3,800 lats.
Misa Peat, a small secondary list company, jumped to 1.01 lats from 0.97 santimes as it saw 9,300 lats of shares change hands.
